4.t: Brother Richard, barber and inventor: block signal, gearshift and torpedo
4.s: Richard barbered by day and invented at night, including a railroad block signal, an automotive gearshift and a guided torpedo the government took.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Richard was a barber, yeah, in his spare time in a... He always had a barber shop where he... He rent a place where he got a big space in the back...

4.t: Richard's rotating barber chair and metal milk-bottle cap
4.s: Richard invented a barber chair that travels around the customer and a metal snap cap for milk bottles that sold widely.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Yeah, so he don't have to stand up. He cut the hair sitting down and travels all around. They tell me they got...my barber up here told me that they got it on the market now, but, you know, this was thirty...forty years ago when his was out. So they say they got one out on the market now that…

4.t: Richard's last invention: a dual hydraulic and electric brake
4.s: Richard spent his earnings on new inventions; his last, a backup electric brake system, came months before he died in 1965.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Well, all of them do. Yeah. All of them do. He had a lot of crazy...now his last invention was...I think I've got the papers in there...I told you that (inaudible) Oh, it says here: His last invention...I got it here somewhere and his papers and everything, and I got letters where some company…

4.t: Richard's patents: milk-bottle opener, tank sampler and gearshift
4.s: Willard reads from a list of Richard Spikes's patents including the milk-bottle cap, a tank sampler sold to Shell and automatic gearshifts.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: [..........] the way I understand it, yeah.

4.t: The automatic bootblack chair and the portable barber chair
4.s: Spikes describes a hydraulic bootblack chair with a shine counter, shown at an inventors' exhibit until the war stopped production, and a bicycle-mounted barber chair.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Here's an automatic bootblack chair that he invented. You see, when this is down--like this--that's the way it stands--these legs out, and say a woman wanted to get on there, she steps on there, and he just shine and press the button and it runs up like this, and the foot pieces come in, and you…

4.t: Richard's patent for a dive-bomber machine gun
4.s: A 1940 patent for a machine gun on ball bearings so a dive bomber could fire in any direction.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Yeah, this fits on, you know, I told you that used to have the old gun that when the airplane would shoot you this way and then they'd have to go 'way around and turn around back and shoot your gun. It was stationary. So he built it on balls and bearin... ball-bearings so that when you pass, you…

4.t: The mitre-box and the water-spraying airplane idea
4.s: Richard's adjustable mitre-box and his earlier notion of an aircraft with a water tank for fighting fires.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: all...you...you put it in there and you twist, and you got it any ...any dimensions you want. If you want a cut an angle like this-- you wanta cut a angle this way or you wanta cut a round angle, you put it in your mitre-box, and you screw it up, and you got it there, and you put your saw in there,…

4.t: The block signal payment, Hiram Johnson and Earl Warren as lawyer
4.s: Richard received about $400,000 for the block signal with backers from Bisbee, got support from Hiram Johnson, and had Earl Warren as lawyer.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Well, yeah, but he got, I think, $400,000, but he had...he had a coupla fellas that were in on that 'cause they gave him money to build it, you know how that is. It was a couple of saloon men in Bisbee, called the Spires Brothers.

4.t: Johnny's writing guide for the blind
4.s: Johnny's only inventions were the Meat Market idea and a writing guide that let blind people write straight lines.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: I said he had a lot of ideas but he never done anything with them. The only thing that Johnny invented was the idea of the Meat Market and the machine--reading for the blind.

4.t: Taking the bootblack chair to New York, 1938-40
4.s: Spikes took Richard's hydraulic bootblack chair to New York to lease it, with hundreds sold before the war killed the project.
4.ch: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
4.q: Oh, I think in...when I took that bootblack chair back there. See? That's about '38 or '39. Y'see, my brother invented it, and what we were gonna do is to lease it, not sell 'em, you see, 'cause we could build them for about twenty-five dollars, and a motor you could get for six or seven…

275.t: Designing the New Look Suit for Men
275.s: He designed a men's suit featured in Look and Life, and describes its cut.
275.q: Yes, I designed a suit shortly after the Second World War, when the ladies' styles came out with the long skirts and dresses. Well, I figured the men should have something keeping in trend with the women, so I designed a suit called the New Look Suit for Men, which was in Look Magazine and Life…
